subject: A quiet week to finish things
preview: A waning moon, Mercury still retrograde, and a question about what's complete.
intro: We start November under a waning moon, the part of the cycle that's made for finishing rather than starting. Mercury and Venus are both still retrograde, so this is a good week to review, tidy up and close open loops before you take on anything new.
outside: Early November light is low and golden. Try ten minutes outside in the late morning, when the sun is at its warmest.
question: What feels finished, even if I haven't admitted it yet?

subject: New moon, and two planets turn forward
preview: The new moon in Scorpio, plus Mercury and Venus end their retrogrades.
intro: Monday's new moon in Scorpio opens a fresh cycle. Then, later in the week, both Mercury and Venus turn direct after weeks of retrograde. If the last month felt like walking through fog, you may feel things start to move again.
outside: Before the week gets busy, step outside on Monday evening. The moon is invisible at the new moon, so it's a good night to notice the stars.
question: What am I ready to begin, now that something old has cleared?

subject: Shooting stars and a shift toward Sagittarius
preview: The Leonid meteor shower peaks, and the Sun moves into Sagittarius on Sunday.
intro: The Leonid meteor shower peaks around Tuesday. Then, next Sunday, the Sun moves from deep, private Scorpio into open, adventurous Sagittarius. Many people feel a lift in their energy as the season tips toward the holidays.
outside: If the sky is clear in the early hours of Tuesday or Wednesday, go somewhere dark and look up for 20 minutes. Bring a blanket.
question: Where in my life do I want more room to breathe?

subject: The Beaver Moon and a softer holiday week
preview: A full moon in Gemini on Tuesday, and permission to go gently this week.
intro: Tuesday brings the Beaver Moon, a full moon in Gemini. Full moons are traditionally a time for completing and releasing. With Thanksgiving this week, that might mean releasing the pressure to make everything perfect.
outside: Take a short walk after the big meal, or step outside on Tuesday evening to see the full moon rise.
question: What do I want to let go of before the holidays begin in earnest?

subject: December arrives with a quieter moon
preview: A waning moon, Venus moves into Scorpio, and Mercury moves into Sagittarius.
intro: December begins under a waning moon, a natural time to slow down and simplify. Venus moves into Scorpio on Friday, and Mercury moves into Sagittarius on Sunday. Think depth in our relationships and a little more optimism in how we talk.
outside: Days are short now. Catch the midday sun when you can: even five minutes on a lunch break counts.
question: What could I take off my plate this month?

subject: New moon in Sagittarius, and the outer planets shift
preview: A new moon on Tuesday, Saturn and Neptune turn direct, and Jupiter turns retrograde.
intro: Tuesday's new moon in Sagittarius is a lovely time to set an intention for the rest of the year, something hopeful and expansive. Later in the week, Saturn and Neptune turn direct while Jupiter begins its retrograde in Leo. It's a lot of movement in the slower-moving planets. Take it as an invitation to check in on your bigger picture.
outside: On a dark, clear night this week, look up. With no moon early in the week, the stars are at their brightest.
question: What do I hope for, really, when I imagine next year?

subject: The Geminids, one of the year's best meteor showers
preview: The Geminid meteor shower peaks on Monday, under a thin crescent moon.
intro: The Geminids peak around Monday night. It's often called one of the best meteor showers of the year, and this year the thin crescent moon sets early, leaving the sky dark. It's a good reminder that even the longest nights of the year hold something bright.
outside: Bundle up, go somewhere dark after 10 pm, and give your eyes 20 minutes to adjust. Wishes optional, but encouraged.
question: What small wonder could I make time for this week?

subject: The longest night, and the light returning
preview: The winter solstice on Monday, and a full Cold Moon in Cancer on Wednesday.
intro: Monday is the winter solstice, the longest night of the year. From here, the light slowly comes back. Then Wednesday brings the full Cold Moon in Cancer, a full moon associated with home, family and comfort, just in time for the holidays.
outside: On the solstice, light a candle at dusk and step outside for a moment to notice how early it's dark. Then notice, over the coming weeks, how the evenings slowly stretch.
question: What am I ready to leave in the dark as the light returns?

subject: The last week of the year
preview: A waning moon to close out the year, and the Quadrantid meteor shower.
intro: The year closes under a waning moon, the part of the cycle meant for reflection and release. There's no rush to have next year figured out. This week is for looking back with kindness. The Quadrantid meteor shower peaks around January 3, a little sparkle to start the new year.
outside: Take a slow walk on New Year's Day morning. Fresh air is a lovely first act of the year.
question: What did this year teach me that I want to remember?

subject: A new moon for the new year
preview: The new moon in Capricorn on Thursday, and Mars turns retrograde.
intro: Thursday's new moon in Capricorn is the real fresh start of the year, a practical, grounded moon that suits steady goals over big dramatic resolutions. Mars turns retrograde in Virgo next Sunday, January 10, and will stay that way until April. It's a reminder to work smarter, not harder.
outside: Morning light is precious in January. Step outside within an hour of waking, even on cloudy days.
question: What one small, steady habit would make this year feel better?

subject: A waxing moon and fresh ideas
preview: The moon grows toward full, and Mercury moves into Aquarius.
intro: The moon is growing this week, a good time to build on the intention you set at the new moon. Mercury moves into Aquarius on Tuesday, a placement associated with fresh ideas, new perspectives and conversations about the future.
outside: Try a morning sun break before work. Five minutes on the porch with your coffee counts.
question: What new idea keeps tapping me on the shoulder?

subject: The Wolf Moon, and Aquarius season begins
preview: The Sun enters Aquarius on Wednesday, and the full Wolf Moon in Leo arrives on Friday.
intro: The Sun moves into Aquarius on Wednesday, the start of a season associated with community and individuality. Then Friday brings the full Wolf Moon in Leo, a warm-hearted full moon that invites you to celebrate what you've grown, and to let your light be seen.
outside: Step outside Friday evening for the moonrise. A full moon over snow, or simply a winter sky, is worth the cold.
question: Where am I hiding my light, and why?

subject: A quiet week under a waning moon
preview: No major shifts in the sky this week: a good week for rest and review.
intro: The sky is quiet this week, with no big shifts, just the moon waning toward next week's new moon. Quiet weeks are underrated. Use this one to rest, finish things and notice how you're really doing three weeks into the year.
outside: Pick one day this week to take a longer walk than usual, without your phone if you can.
question: How am I actually doing, beneath the busyness?

subject: Eclipse season begins
preview: An annular solar eclipse on Saturday, at the new moon in Aquarius.
intro: Saturday's new moon in Aquarius is also an annular solar eclipse. The moon passes in front of the sun and leaves a 'ring of fire' around it, visible from southern South America and parts of Africa. In astrology, eclipses are traditionally seen as turning points. Treat it as a prompt to notice what's shifting, not a prediction. Mercury retrograde begins next week, so this is a good time to get your plans in order.
outside: Even though the eclipse isn't visible from the US, take a moment on Saturday to step outside and notice the light. Never look at the sun directly.
question: What turning point have I been sensing in my life lately?

subject: Mercury retrograde begins
preview: Uranus turns direct, and Mercury begins its first retrograde of the year on Tuesday.
intro: Mercury turns retrograde in Pisces on Tuesday and stays retrograde until March 3. It's the first of three retrogrades this year. Uranus also turns direct on Monday. Use this retrograde for reviewing, revising and reconnecting rather than launching. Our blog has all three of this year's retrograde dates.
outside: Pisces season is coming. Find some water this week: a creek, a lake, a fountain or a long bath.
question: What do I want to revisit, rather than rush past?

subject: A lunar eclipse at the full moon
preview: The Sun enters Pisces, and Saturday's full Snow Moon in Virgo is also a penumbral lunar eclipse.
intro: The Sun moves into Pisces on Thursday. Then Saturday's full Snow Moon in Virgo is also a penumbral lunar eclipse, a subtle shading as the moon passes through the outer edge of Earth's shadow. It closes this eclipse season. Virgo full moons are good for looking at your daily routines and what needs adjusting.
outside: Go outside on Saturday evening to see the full moon rise. The eclipse is best seen from Europe, Africa and Asia, but the moon is lovely either way.
question: What everyday habit is quietly draining me?

subject: After the eclipse, a gentle week
preview: A waning moon and a quiet sky: time to rest and integrate.
intro: After the eclipse, the sky goes quiet. The moon wanes all week. Mercury is still retrograde, so this is a good week to slow down, finish things and let the last few weeks settle.
outside: As the days lengthen, notice when the sun sets now compared with December. It's a little later every week.
question: What has shifted for me since the start of February?

subject: Mercury moves forward again
preview: Venus enters Aquarius on Monday, and Mercury turns direct on Wednesday.
intro: Mercury turns direct in Aquarius on Wednesday, ending the first retrograde of the year. Venus moves into Aquarius too. If conversations, plans or tech have felt tangled lately, things may start to flow more easily now. It's a good time to act on what you reviewed.
outside: Spring is starting to stir in many places. Look for the first green shoots on a walk this week.
question: What did I learn during the retrograde that I want to act on now?

subject: A new moon in Pisces
preview: Monday's new moon in Pisces: a dreamy, gentle fresh start.
intro: Monday's new moon in Pisces is the last new moon of the astrological year, a soft, imaginative moon associated with dreams, compassion and rest. It's a good time for an intention about kindness, creativity or simply letting yourself rest more.
outside: The ground is warming in many places. If you can, try a couple of minutes barefoot on the grass this week.
question: What would I do with my time if I trusted that resting is allowed?

preview: Saturday is the spring equinox, when day and night are nearly equal.
intro: Saturday is the spring equinox. Day and night are nearly equal, and the Sun moves into Aries, the start of the astrological new year. Mercury also moves into Pisces on Thursday. It's a natural moment for a balance check: rest and work, giving and receiving, others and yourself.
outside: Mark the equinox outside. Watch the sunrise or sunset, and notice how much light has returned since December.
question: Which area of my life most needs rebalancing this spring?

outside: The ground is waking up. Spend a few minutes with your hands in garden soil, or your feet on spring grass.
question: Which relationship needs a little more balance?

intro: Mars, the planet associated with energy, drive and courage, turns direct on Thursday after a long retrograde that began in January. Projects that stalled may start to move again. The moon is waning, so ease in: finish what's in front of you before charging ahead.
outside: Barefoot season is starting in many places. Try five minutes on the grass this week.
question: What have I been waiting to have the energy for?

subject: A new moon in Aries

Mercury follows the Sun into Aries on Thursday. If there's something you've been wanting to begin, this is a good week to take the first step.
outside: Start the week outside: a sunrise walk is a lovely way to mark a new moon.
question: What brave first step have I been putting off?

outside: Spring evenings are getting longer. Take a walk after dinner and enjoy the extra light.
question: Where in my life do I want to grow?

question: Who mothered me in ways I don't often acknowledge?

question: What am I curious about right now?

question: What daily routine would help me grow this year?

subject: The great total solar eclipse
preview: Monday's new moon in Leo is a total solar eclipse, one of the longest of the century.
intro: Monday's new moon in Leo is a total solar eclipse. Its path crosses Spain, North Africa and the Middle East, with more than six minutes of totality near Luxor, Egypt. It isn't visible from the US, but it's a powerful marker in the year's sky. In astrology, solar eclipses are often described as a new moon with the volume turned up: a prompt for big, brave beginnings, not a prediction. Mercury also enters Leo on Monday.
outside: Wherever you are on Monday, step outside and notice the daylight. Never look directly at the sun.
question: What brave new beginning is asking for my attention?

outside: Plan a Perseid night: a dark spot, a blanket, and an hour of looking up after midnight.
question: What do I wish for, for myself, someone I love and the world?

outside: If you're up early on Tuesday, step out and look at the full moon. Notice if one side looks slightly dimmer.
question: What community or group do I want to belong to more fully?

question: What small change would make my days run more smoothly?

outside: Watch the Harvest Moon rise just after sunset on Wednesday. It often looks big and golden near the horizon.
question: What did I harvest this year, including the hard-won things?

question: What am I ready to let fall away?

outside: Crisp mornings are here. Bundle up and take your coffee outside.

question: Who or what am I remembering this season?

subject: A new moon to close the year's circle

question: Who have I become this year?
